questions.q: A hollow metallic sphere of radius R carries a charge Q. What is the electric potential at its centre?
questions.explanation: The field inside a conductor is zero, so the potential is constant throughout the inside and equals the surface value kQ/R.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor stays connected to a battery. A dielectric slab of constant K = 4 is then inserted to fill the gap completely. The energy stored in the capacitor becomes
questions.explanation: With V fixed, capacitance becomes 4C, and U = (1/2)CV^2 becomes four times the original value.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Define the electric dipole moment. State its direction and SI unit.
questions.answer: Electric dipole moment is the product of the magnitude of either charge and the separation between the two charges. It is a vector pointing from the negative charge to the positive charge, and its SI unit is coulomb metre (C m).
questions.explanation: A dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges separated by a small distance, and p describes its strength and orientation.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Why is the electric field inside a conductor zero in electrostatic conditions?
questions.answer: Free charges in a conductor move until the net field inside is cancelled. If any field existed, free charges would keep moving, so in the static state the field must be zero, the excess charge sits on the surface and the field just outside is perpendicular to the surface.
keyPoints: Free charges rearrange under any field
Rearrangement stops only when net field is zero
Excess charge resides on the surface
questions.explanation: Static equilibrium means no net force on free charges, which requires zero field inside the conductor.

questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohm; siemens is the unit of conductance.

questions.explanation: For equal resistors in parallel R_eq = R/n = 6/3 = 2 ohm.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity perpendicular to the field. Which quantity of the particle remains constant?
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity so it does no work; speed and kinetic energy stay constant while the direction keeps changing.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: A uniform wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly to double its length, its volume remaining the same. Its new resistance is
questions.explanation: Length doubles and area halves, so R = rho L/A becomes (2L)/(A/2) times rho, that is 4R.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: State Kirchhoff's two rules for electric circuits.
questions.answer: The junction rule says the algebraic sum of currents meeting at a junction is zero (charge is conserved). The loop rule says the algebraic sum of potential differences around any closed loop is zero (energy is conserved).
keyPoints: Junction rule: sum of currents at a junction is zero
Loop rule: sum of potential changes in a closed loop is zero
Based on conservation of charge and energy
questions.explanation: These rules let us analyse circuits that cannot be reduced by simple series-parallel combinations.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter, and why must the ammeter have a low resistance?
questions.answer: A small resistance called a shunt is connected in parallel with the galvanometer so most of the current bypasses the coil. The ammeter is connected in series in the circuit, and its resistance must be very low so that it does not change the current it is measuring.
keyPoints: Low-resistance shunt in parallel with galvanometer
Low resistance so the circuit current is hardly disturbed
questions.explanation: The shunt carries most of the current and the combined resistance is smaller than that of the shunt.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: According to Faraday's law, the emf induced in a coil is proportional to
options: the rate of change of magnetic flux through it
the total magnetic flux through it
the current already in the coil
questions.explanation: Induced emf equals the negative of the rate of change of magnetic flux linked with the coil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of inductance is
questions.explanation: Inductance is measured in henry (H); weber is the unit of magnetic flux and tesla of magnetic field.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: emf = change in flux / time = 0.06/0.3 = 0.2 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Suppose the induced current in a loop aided the change in flux that produced it, instead of opposing it. Which principle would be violated?
questions.explanation: Aiding the change would increase the flux further and produce unlimited current from no input, creating energy from nothing; Lenz's law is an expression of energy conservation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a transformer and on what principle does it work?
questions.answer: A transformer is a device that increases or decreases an alternating voltage. It works on the principle of mutual induction between two coils wound on a common iron core.
keyPoints: Changes AC voltage up or down
Primary and secondary coils on a common core
questions.explanation: A changing flux produced by the primary induces an emf in the secondary.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does an ideal inductor connected to an AC source not consume any average power?
questions.answer: In a purely inductive circuit the current lags the voltage by 90 degrees. Power is positive for one quarter of the cycle and negative for the next quarter, so the average power over a full cycle is zero.
keyPoints: Average power over a cycle is zero
questions.explanation: Energy is stored in the magnetic field and returned to the source each cycle.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of light at the boundary of two media due to the change in its speed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of the power of a lens is
questions.explanation: Power is 1/f with f in metres and is measured in dioptre (D).

questions.explanation: From 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = -30 and f = -15, 1/v = -1/15 + 1/30 = -1/30, so v = -30 cm: the image is at the centre of curvature.

questions.explanation: Wavelength in water is smaller than in air, and fringe width = lambda D/d is proportional to the wavelength, so it decreases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The critical angle for glass-air is about 42 degrees. In which case can total internal reflection occur?
options: light going from air to glass at 80 degrees
light going from glass to air at 30 degrees
light going from glass to air at 60 degrees
light going from air to water at 89 degrees
questions.explanation: TIR needs light travelling from the denser to the rarer medium with an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle; only 60 degrees glass to air satisfies this.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is diffraction of light, and when is it most noticeable?
questions.answer: Diffraction is the bending of light around the edges of an obstacle or aperture so that it spreads into the geometrical shadow. It is most noticeable when the size of the obstacle or slit is comparable to the wavelength of light.
keyPoints: Bending or spreading of light at edges or slits
Size of aperture comparable to wavelength
questions.explanation: Single-slit patterns with a central bright maximum are a standard example.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a glass convex lens behave like a diverging lens when it is immersed in a liquid of higher refractive index than glass?
questions.answer: The behaviour depends on the refractive index of the lens relative to the surrounding medium. If the surrounding liquid has a higher index than glass, light bends away from the normal on entering the lens and the relative index is below 1, so the focal length changes sign and the lens diverges.
keyPoints: Relative index of glass to liquid is less than 1
Sign of focal length reverses so lens diverges
questions.explanation: From the lens-maker's formula, 1/f is proportional to (n_lens/n_medium - 1), which becomes negative.

options: the maximum kinetic energy of electrons doubles
questions.explanation: Doubling intensity doubles the number of photons and hence the emitted electrons, while the maximum kinetic energy depends only on frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Why does the fusion of two light nuclei release energy?
options: the product nucleus has a lower binding energy per nucleon
the product has no mass defect
the number of neutrons always decreases
the product nucleus has a higher binding energy per nucleon
questions.explanation: Light nuclei lie on the rising part of the binding energy curve, so fusion gives a more tightly bound nucleus and the difference is released as energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Define half-life of a radioactive substance and write its relation with the decay constant.
questions.answer: Half-life is the time in which half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample decay. It is related to the decay constant by T_half = 0.693/lambda.
keyPoints: Time for half the nuclei to decay
questions.explanation: It follows from N = N0 e^(-lambda t) by setting N = N0/2.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V.
questions.answer: Using lambda = h/sqrt(2 m e V) = 12.27/sqrt(V) angstrom, with V = 100 V the wavelength is about 1.23 angstrom (0.123 nm).
questions.explanation: The wavelength is comparable to atomic spacings, which is why electrons show diffraction from crystals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Molarity of a solution is defined as the number of moles of solute present in
questions.explanation: Molarity = moles of solute per litre of solution; moles per kg of solvent is molality.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a galvanic cell, reduction takes place at the
questions.explanation: The cathode is where reduction occurs and the anode is where oxidation occurs, in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

questions.explanation: Moles = 4/40 = 0.1 mol; molarity = 0.1/0.5 L = 0.2 M.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A current of 2 A is passed through CuSO4 solution for 965 s. What mass of copper is deposited? (Cu = 63.5 g/mol, F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Charge = 1930 C = 0.02 mol of electrons; Cu2+ needs 2 electrons so 0.01 mol Cu = 0.635 g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Raoult's law for a solution of volatile liquids.
questions.answer: For a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution, p_A = x_A p_A^0, and the total vapour pressure is the sum of the partial pressures.
keyPoints: Partial pressure proportional to mole fraction
p_A = x_A times vapour pressure of pure A
Total pressure is sum of partial pressures
questions.explanation: Solutions obeying this law over the whole range of composition are called ideal solutions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does the molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte rise sharply on dilution?
questions.answer: On dilution the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte increases, giving more ions in solution for the same amount of electrolyte. This increase in ions outweighs the fall in concentration, so molar conductivity rises steeply.
keyPoints: More ions per mole of electrolyte
questions.explanation: Molar conductivity is conductivity per unit concentration, and the ion count per mole increases on dilution.

questions.explanation: For first order, rate = k[A], so k has units of s^-1.

questions.q: Which of the following is a d-block element?
questions.explanation: Iron has its last electron in the 3d subshell, whereas Na and Ca are s-block and Al is p-block.

questions.explanation: K is +1 and four oxygens give -8, so Mn must be +7.

questions.q: For a reaction with rate = k[A]^2[B], the concentrations of both A and B are doubled. The rate becomes
questions.explanation: Rate changes by 2^2 × 2 = 8 times.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Which aqueous ion is colourless?
questions.explanation: Zn2+ has a completely filled 3d10 configuration with no d-d transitions possible; the others have partly filled d orbitals and are coloured.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: What is activation energy? How does a catalyst affect it?
questions.answer: Activation energy is the minimum extra energy that reacting molecules must have for a collision to result in a reaction. A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, so more molecules can react and the rate increases.
keyPoints: Minimum energy needed for effective collisions
Lower activation energy raises the rate
questions.explanation: In the Arrhenius equation k = A e^(-Ea/RT), a smaller Ea gives a larger k.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: What is lanthanoid contraction and what is one of its consequences?
questions.answer: Lanthanoid contraction is the steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium, caused by poor shielding of the nuclear charge by the 4f electrons. As a result, zirconium and hafnium have almost the same radii and are very similar in properties.
keyPoints: Gradual decrease in size across the 4f series
Zr and Hf very similar, hard to separate
questions.explanation: Each added 4f electron shields poorly, so the effective nuclear charge pulls the outer electrons in.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the complex ion [Fe(CN)6]4-, the ligand is
questions.explanation: The cyanide ions are the ligands bonded to the central iron(II) ion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The coordination number of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]3+ is
questions.explanation: Six monodentate ammonia ligands are bonded to the cobalt ion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The oxidation state of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 is
questions.explanation: NH3 is neutral and three chloride ions are outside the complex, so the complex cation is 3+ and cobalt is +3.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of K4[Fe(CN)6] is
questions.explanation: Four K+ balance a 4- complex anion; with six CN- the iron is +2, so the name is potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many geometrical isomers does the octahedral ion [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ have?
questions.explanation: The two chloride ligands can be adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans), giving two geometrical isomers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about [Ni(CO)4] is correct?
options: it is square planar and paramagnetic
it is square planar and diamagnetic
questions.explanation: Nickel is in the zero oxidation state (3d10) with sp3 hybridisation, giving a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a ligand? Give one example each of a monodentate and a bidentate ligand.
questions.answer: A ligand is an ion or molecule that donates a lone pair of electrons to the central metal atom or ion to form a coordinate bond. NH3 or Cl- is monodentate, while ethane-1,2-diamine or oxalate is bidentate.
keyPoints: Donates a lone pair to the central metal
questions.explanation: Denticity is the number of donor atoms through which a ligand binds to the metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does a coordination compound differ from a double salt? Give an example of each.
questions.answer: A double salt such as carnallite or Mohr's salt breaks up completely into its simple ions in water and loses its identity. A coordination compound such as K4[Fe(CN)6] keeps the complex ion intact in solution and does not give the test for the central metal ion.
keyPoints: Double salt dissociates completely into simple ions
Complex ion retains its identity in solution
questions.explanation: In the complex the ligands are bonded to the metal by coordinate bonds, so it behaves as a single unit.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl (-OH) group attached to a saturated carbon.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2Br is
questions.explanation: A two-carbon chain with one bromine is named bromoethane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon proceeds with
options: no change in the carbon skeleton or geometry
questions.explanation: The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, inverting the configuration in a single step.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanol heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K mainly gives
questions.explanation: At 443 K with excess acid the main product is ethene by dehydration; diethyl ether forms at about 413 K with excess alcohol.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which alkyl chloride reacts fastest by the SN1 mechanism?
questions.explanation: SN1 proceeds through a carbocation, and the tertiary carbocation from tert-butyl chloride is the most stable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol mainly because
options: the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
phenol forms stronger hydrogen bonds with itself
the O-H bond in phenol is non-polar
questions.explanation: The negative charge on the phenoxide ion is delocalised into the benzene ring, which stabilises it and favours loss of H+.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can ethyl methyl ether be prepared by Williamson synthesis?
questions.answer: Sodium ethoxide is reacted with bromomethane (or sodium methoxide with bromoethane): C2H5ONa + CH3Br gives C2H5OCH3 + NaBr. It is an SN2 reaction between an alkoxide and a primary alkyl halide.
keyPoints: SN2 reaction with a primary halide
questions.explanation: A primary alkyl halide is used because secondary or tertiary halides would mainly undergo elimination.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do alcohols have much higher boiling points than haloalkanes or ethers of comparable molar mass?
questions.answer: Alcohol molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through the O-H group, which need extra energy to break. Haloalkanes and ethers cannot hydrogen-bond with themselves, so their boiling points are lower.
keyPoints: Extra energy needed to break them
Ethers and haloalkanes lack O-H bonding
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding is much stronger than the dipole-dipole forces in ethers and haloalkanes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The functional group of an aldehyde is
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain the -CHO (formyl) group.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A silver mirror is formed on warming an aldehyde with
questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) is reduced to silver metal by aldehydes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oxidation of ethanal gives
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are readily oxidised to carboxylic acids with the same number of carbon atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Glucose is classified as a
questions.explanation: Glucose has six carbons and an aldehyde group, making it an aldohexose and a monosaccharide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these gives a positive iodoform test?
questions.explanation: Propanone has a CH3-CO- group, which is required for the iodoform reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aniline is a weaker base than ethylamine because
options: the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring
questions.explanation: Delocalisation of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring makes it less available to accept a proton.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a peptide bond?
questions.answer: A peptide bond is the amide linkage (-CO-NH-) formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, with loss of a water molecule. Many such bonds join amino acids into peptides and proteins.
keyPoints: Between carboxyl of one and amino group of another amino acid
questions.explanation: Chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds make up proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is sucrose a non-reducing sugar?
questions.answer: In sucrose the C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose are joined through a glycosidic bond, so both potential carbonyl groups are tied up. There is no free aldehyde or ketone group, so sucrose does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent.
keyPoints: Glycosidic link between C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose
No free aldehyde or ketone group
Does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent
questions.explanation: Reducing sugars must have a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group that can open to give a carbonyl.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sperms are produced in the
questions.explanation: The testes contain seminiferous tubules in which sperms are formed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The sperm meets the ovum in the ampullary region of the oviduct, and the zygote then moves to the uterus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The surge of which hormone triggers ovulation in the human menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: A mid-cycle LH surge causes the Graafian follicle to rupture and release the ovum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In which part of the testis does spermatogenesis take place?
questions.explanation: Spermatogonia in the seminiferous tubules divide and differentiate into sperms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In flowering plants, the primary endosperm nucleus is triploid because it forms by the fusion of
options: one male gamete with the egg
two male gametes with the egg
one male gamete with two polar nuclei
one male gamete with one synergid
questions.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (2n together) in triple fusion, giving a 3n nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: After a man undergoes vasectomy, which function continues normally?
options: passage of sperms through the vas deferens
presence of sperms in the semen
questions.explanation: Vasectomy only cuts the vas deferens; the Leydig cells keep secreting testosterone, so secondary sexual characters are unaffected.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is double fertilisation in flowering plants?
questions.answer: In double fertilisation, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form the diploid zygote (syngamy), while the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (triple fusion). It is characteristic of angiosperms.
keyPoints: Triple fusion forms the primary endosperm nucleus
questions.explanation: The zygote develops into the embryo and the endosperm nucleus into food-storing tissue.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe how the placenta allows exchange between mother and foetus even though their bloods do not mix.
questions.answer: The placenta has villi where foetal capillaries lie close to maternal blood spaces separated by thin membranes. Oxygen, nutrients and antibodies diffuse into the foetal blood while carbon dioxide and wastes pass to the mother, with the two blood supplies kept separate.
keyPoints: Thin membrane between foetal and maternal blood
Oxygen and nutrients pass to foetus
Wastes and CO2 pass to mother
questions.explanation: The placenta also secretes hormones such as hCG, oestrogen and progesterone.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: The sex chromosomes of a normal human female are
questions.explanation: Females are XX and males are XY.

questions.q: What is a codon? Which codon starts translation and what amino acid does it code for?
questions.answer: A codon is a sequence of three adjacent nucleotides on mRNA that codes for one amino acid or a stop signal. The start codon is AUG, which codes for methionine.
questions.explanation: The genetic code is read in non-overlapping triplets.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Explain with the example of peppered moths how natural selection can change a population.
questions.answer: Before industrialisation light-coloured moths were camouflaged on lichen-covered bark and survived better. When soot darkened the bark, dark moths escaped predators more easily and their proportion increased, showing selection of the variant better suited to the changed environment.
keyPoints: Proportion of the better-adapted form increased
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on existing variation and changes allele frequencies over generations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Enzymes that cut DNA at specific recognition sequences are called
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors in recombinant DNA technology.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The heat-stable enzyme Taq polymerase used in PCR was isolated from
questions.explanation: Taq polymerase comes from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus and survives the high temperature of denaturation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: According to the ten per cent law, if producers fix 10 000 J of energy, the energy available to the herbivores is about
questions.explanation: About 10% of the energy passes to the next trophic level, so 1000 J reaches herbivores.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bt cotton is protected against attack by
questions.explanation: It carries a Bacillus thuringiensis gene for a toxin that kills the larvae of cotton bollworms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Excess fertiliser run-off into a lake leads to eutrophication. Which sequence correctly describes the effect?
options: nutrient rise, algal bloom, fall in dissolved oxygen, fish deaths
nutrient fall, algal decline, rise in oxygen, more fish
nutrient rise, rise in oxygen, more fish
nutrient rise, fall in algae, fall in temperature
questions.explanation: Extra nutrients cause an algal bloom; its decomposition uses up dissolved oxygen, killing aquatic animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why can the pyramid of numbers be inverted in a forest ecosystem with one large tree supporting many insects?
options: the pyramid of energy is also inverted
trees consume more energy than insects
producers are fewer in number but each is very large
questions.explanation: Numbers ignore body size, so a single large producer can support many consumers; the energy pyramid is still upright.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the three types of ecological pyramids.
questions.answer: The three ecological pyramids are the pyramid of numbers, the pyramid of biomass and the pyramid of energy. Only the pyramid of energy is always upright.
questions.explanation: Energy decreases at each trophic level because of loss as heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What roles do DNA ligase and a plasmid vector play in making recombinant DNA?
questions.answer: A plasmid vector carries the foreign gene into a host cell and replicates there. DNA ligase joins the cut ends of the foreign DNA and the plasmid by forming phosphodiester bonds, giving a recombinant molecule.
keyPoints: Plasmid carries and replicates the gene in the host
Ligase seals nicks by joining DNA fragments
questions.explanation: Both fragment and vector are first cut with the same restriction enzyme to give compatible ends.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Electric field lines due to an isolated positive point charge
options: start at the charge and go outwards
form closed loops around the charge
cross each other near the charge
questions.explanation: Field lines begin on positive charges and end on negative charges; they never cross and are not closed loops.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: The SI unit of capacitance is
questions.explanation: One farad equals one coulomb per volt.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: When a glass rod is rubbed with silk, the rod becomes positively charged because
options: protons move from silk to glass
protons move from glass to silk
electrons move from silk to glass
electrons move from glass to silk
questions.explanation: Only electrons are transferred in charging by friction; the glass loses electrons and becomes positive.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: The separation between the plates of an air-filled parallel-plate capacitor is doubled, with the plate area unchanged. Its capacitance
questions.explanation: C = epsilon_0 A/d is inversely proportional to d, so doubling d halves C.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: An electric dipole is placed in a uniform electric field with its axis at an angle to the field. The dipole experiences
options: a net force but no torque
both a net force and a torque
a torque but no net force
questions.explanation: The forces on the two charges are equal and opposite so the net force is zero, but they act at different points and produce a torque p × E.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: State Gauss's law in electrostatics.
questions.answer: The total electric flux through any closed surface is equal to the net charge enclosed by the surface divided by epsilon_0, that is, flux = q_enclosed/epsilon_0.
keyPoints: Flux depends on enclosed charge only
questions.explanation: It is useful for finding fields of symmetrical charge distributions.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A point charge is at the centre of a spherical Gaussian surface. If the radius of the sphere is doubled, how does the electric flux through it change? Explain.
questions.answer: The flux does not change. By Gauss's law the flux depends only on the charge enclosed, which stays the same. The field at the surface falls to one fourth but the area becomes four times as large, so the product is unchanged.
keyPoints: Field falls by 1/4 while area rises 4 times
questions.explanation: This also shows that the inverse-square nature of the field is consistent with Gauss's law.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: An ammeter is connected in a circuit
options: either way with the same result
questions.explanation: An ammeter must carry the same current as the component and has a very low resistance.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic field is
questions.explanation: Magnetic field (flux density) is measured in tesla; one tesla is one weber per square metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 ohm is connected to an external resistance of 5 ohm. The terminal voltage of the cell is
questions.explanation: I = 12/(5 + 1) = 2 A; terminal voltage = E - Ir = 12 - 2 = 10 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: The speed of a charged particle moving in a circle in a uniform magnetic field is doubled. The time period of its revolution
questions.explanation: The period T = 2 pi m/(qB) does not depend on speed, since the radius also doubles.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: State Ohm's law.
questions.answer: At constant temperature the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, V = IR, where R is the resistance of the conductor.
keyPoints: At constant temperature and physical conditions
questions.explanation: The law holds for ohmic conductors such as metals at fixed temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Why are alloys like manganin or constantan used to make standard resistors?
questions.answer: These alloys have a high resistivity and a very small temperature coefficient of resistance, so their resistance stays almost constant when the wire heats up and a compact coil can give a large resistance.
questions.explanation: Pure metals show a noticeable rise in resistance with temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An AC generator converts
options: heat energy into mechanical energy only
questions.explanation: A rotating coil in a magnetic field produces an induced emf, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The direction of the induced current in a closed loop is given by
questions.explanation: Lenz's law says the induced current opposes the change in flux that produces it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A step-down transformer has 2200 turns in the primary and 100 turns in the secondary. If the input is 220 V, the output voltage is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The frequency of the domestic AC supply in India is
questions.explanation: Mains electricity in India is supplied at 50 Hz.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When the frequency of an AC source is increased, the reactance of a capacitor
questions.explanation: X_C = 1/(2 pi f C) falls as f rises, whereas inductive reactance X_L = 2 pi f L rises.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of turns of a long solenoid is doubled while its length and area stay the same. Its self-inductance becomes
questions.explanation: L = mu_0 N^2 A/l is proportional to N^2, so doubling N gives four times the inductance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Lenz's law and give one everyday consequence of it.
questions.answer: Lenz's law states that the polarity of the induced emf is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it. For example, a magnet dropped through a copper tube falls slowly because eddy currents oppose its motion.
keyPoints: Induced current opposes the change in flux
Example such as magnet falling slowly in a conducting tube
questions.explanation: The negative sign in Faraday's law expresses Lenz's law.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are the iron cores of transformers made of thin insulated sheets instead of a solid block?
questions.answer: A solid core has large eddy currents induced in it by the changing flux, which waste energy as heat. Thin laminations insulated from each other break up the paths of these currents and greatly reduce the loss.
keyPoints: Laminations cut down the current paths
questions.explanation: A soft iron core is also used to keep hysteresis loss low.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as the rear-view mirror of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wide field of view.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Among the visible colours, the one with the longest wavelength is
questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) and violet the shortest.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Its power is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f with f = 0.2 m gives +5 dioptre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray in air strikes a glass slab at 45 degrees and refracts at 30 degrees to the normal. The refractive index of the glass is about

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is placed between F and 2F of a convex lens. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and of the same size at 2F
questions.explanation: For an object between F and 2F the image is real, inverted, magnified and lies beyond 2F on the other side.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a single-slit diffraction experiment the slit width is made smaller. The central maximum
questions.explanation: The angular width of the central maximum is about 2 lambda/a, so a smaller slit width a gives a wider pattern.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is total internal reflection? State its two conditions and one application.
questions.answer: Total internal reflection is the complete reflection of light back into the denser medium at the boundary with a rarer medium. It needs light going from denser to rarer medium and an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle. It is used in optical fibres.
keyPoints: Light travels from denser to rarer medium
Angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle
Application such as optical fibres or prisms
questions.explanation: No refracted ray exists beyond the critical angle, so all the light is reflected.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does the Sun look reddish at sunrise and sunset?
questions.answer: At these times sunlight travels a longer path through the atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths such as blue are scattered away much more strongly (scattering varies as 1/lambda^4), so mostly the longer red wavelengths reach the observer.
questions.explanation: This is Rayleigh scattering, which also explains the blue colour of the sky.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The nucleus of an atom was discovered through the scattering experiment of
questions.explanation: Geiger and Marsden's alpha-particle scattering experiment led Rutherford to propose the nuclear atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Photons of energy 3.1 eV fall on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is
questions.explanation: K_max = hf - phi = 3.1 - 2.0 = 1.1 eV.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: After one alpha decay, the nucleus of uranium-238 (atomic number 92) becomes
questions.explanation: An alpha particle carries away 2 protons and 2 neutrons, so mass number falls by 4 and atomic number by 2.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A sample has 8000 radioactive nuclei and its half-life is 10 days. The number of undecayed nuclei after 30 days is
questions.explanation: 30 days is 3 half-lives, so the number left is 8000/2^3 = 1000.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: An electron and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Which has the longer de Broglie wavelength?
questions.explanation: lambda = h/sqrt(2mK), so for the same K the lighter particle, the electron, has the longer wavelength.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Write Einstein's photoelectric equation and explain each term.
questions.answer: The equation is K_max = h f - phi. Here h f is the energy of the incident photon, phi is the work function (minimum energy to free an electron from the metal) and K_max is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron.
questions.explanation: Emission occurs only when hf is greater than or equal to phi, which gives the threshold frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Why are neutrons more effective than protons or alpha particles for inducing nuclear reactions?
questions.answer: Neutrons carry no charge, so they feel no electrostatic repulsion from the positively charged nucleus. Even slow neutrons can approach and enter the nucleus, while charged particles need high energy to overcome the Coulomb barrier.
keyPoints: No Coulomb repulsion from the nucleus
questions.explanation: This is why thermal neutrons are used to induce fission of uranium-235.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a colligative property?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles; osmotic pressure is one of the four.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of molality is
questions.explanation: Molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The molality of a solution prepared by dissolving 18 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) in 500 g of water is
questions.explanation: Moles = 18/180 = 0.1; mass of solvent = 0.5 kg; molality = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 m.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The standard electrode potential of the standard hydrogen electrode is taken as
questions.explanation: By convention the SHE is assigned zero potential at all temperatures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Given E° (Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V and E° (Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V, the standard emf of the Zn-Cu galvanic cell is
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bubbles of gas rush out when a soda bottle is opened mainly because
options: the pressure above the liquid drops and gas solubility falls
the temperature of the drink falls suddenly
carbon dioxide reacts with the cap
questions.explanation: By Henry's law the solubility of a gas is proportional to its pressure, so releasing the pressure lets dissolved gas escape.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Faraday's first law of electrolysis.
questions.answer: The mass of a substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of charge passed through the electrolyte, m = Z I t.
questions.explanation: Charge equals current multiplied by time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is osmotic pressure preferred over the other colligative properties for finding the molar mass of proteins and polymers?
questions.answer: Osmotic pressure can be measured at room temperature, so heat-sensitive biomolecules are not damaged. It also gives a large, easily measured value even for very dilute solutions, whereas the other colligative effects are too small to measure accurately for large molecules.
keyPoints: Large value even at low concentration
questions.explanation: Large molecules have a very small mole fraction even at appreciable mass concentration.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The order of a reaction is
options: the sum of the powers of the concentration terms in the rate law
the number of molecules in the balanced equation
always a whole number from 1 to 3
questions.explanation: Order is found from experiment as the sum of the exponents of concentrations in the rate law.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The most common oxidation state of the lanthanoids is
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids characteristically show the +3 oxidation state.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: For a zero-order reaction k = 0.02 mol L^-1 s^-1. How long does it take for the concentration to fall from 0.5 M to 0.3 M?
questions.explanation: For zero order [A]0 - [A] = kt, so t = 0.2/0.02 = 10 s.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The oxidation state of chromium in potassium dichromate, K2Cr2O7, is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The rate of many reactions roughly doubles for a 10 K rise in temperature mainly because
options: a larger fraction of molecules has energy equal to or above the activation energy
questions.explanation: A small rise in temperature increases the fraction of molecules crossing the energy barrier substantially.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is
questions.explanation: A half-filled d subshell gives extra stability, so one 4s electron moves to 3d.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Distinguish between the order and the molecularity of a reaction.
questions.answer: Order is found experimentally from the rate law and can be zero, fractional or whole. Molecularity is the number of reacting species colliding in an elementary step; it is always a whole number and applies only to elementary reactions.
keyPoints: Order is experimental, can be fractional or zero
Molecularity refers to an elementary step
questions.explanation: For complex reactions the slowest step determines the rate.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Why do transition metals show variable oxidation states and act as good catalysts?
questions.answer: The (n-1)d and ns electrons have nearly the same energy, so different numbers of electrons can be used in bonding, giving variable oxidation states. They can also form unstable intermediates and offer surfaces for adsorption, which lets them act as catalysts.
keyPoints: Small energy gap between ns and (n-1)d
Intermediates and adsorption sites help catalysis
questions.explanation: Vanadium(V) oxide in the contact process and iron in the Haber process are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The coordination theory of complex compounds was proposed by
questions.explanation: Alfred Werner proposed primary and secondary valences to explain complexes of cobalt.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: EDTA is a
questions.explanation: EDTA binds through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms, so it is hexadentate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The formula of tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride is
questions.explanation: Four NH3 and two Cl- are inside the bracket; Co(III) with two Cl- leaves a 1+ cation balanced by one outer Cl-.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of unpaired electrons in the low-spin complex [Fe(CN)6]4- is
questions.explanation: Fe2+ is d6; the strong-field CN- ligands pair all electrons in the t2g orbitals, so the complex is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in the high-spin complex [CoF6]3-?
questions.explanation: Co3+ is d6 and F- is a weak-field ligand, so the electrons occupy t2g^4 eg^2 with four unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following octahedral complexes shows optical isomerism?
questions.explanation: [Co(en)3]3+ has no plane of symmetry, so it exists as non-superimposable mirror-image forms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the spectrochemical series? Arrange I-, H2O and CN- in order of increasing field strength.
questions.answer: The spectrochemical series arranges ligands in order of the extent to which they split the d orbitals of the central metal. In increasing order of field strength: I- < H2O < CN-.
keyPoints: Ligands ordered by crystal field splitting power
questions.explanation: Strong-field ligands give a large splitting and favour low-spin complexes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: [Ni(CN)4]2- is diamagnetic but [NiCl4]2- is paramagnetic. Explain.
questions.answer: CN- is a strong-field ligand that pairs the d electrons of Ni2+, giving dsp2 hybridisation and a square planar diamagnetic complex. Cl- is weak-field and cannot pair them, so Ni2+ uses sp3 hybridisation with two unpaired electrons in a tetrahedral paramagnetic complex.
keyPoints: CN- pairs electrons, dsp2, square planar
Cl- leaves two unpaired electrons, sp3, tetrahedral
questions.explanation: The nature of the ligand decides both the geometry and the magnetic behaviour.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The general formula of a saturated monohaloalkane is
questions.explanation: A haloalkane is an alkane in which one hydrogen is replaced by a halogen, giving CnH2n+1X.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an ether?
questions.explanation: Ethers contain a C-O-C linkage; CH3OCH3 is methoxymethane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the Lucas test, which alcohol gives turbidity immediately at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react at once with Lucas reagent (ZnCl2 and conc. HCl) because they form stable carbocations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Phenol on treatment with bromine water gives a white precipitate of
questions.explanation: The -OH group strongly activates the ring, so all three ortho and para positions are brominated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Chlorobenzene is much less reactive than chloroethane towards nucleophilic substitution mainly because
options: it has a larger molar mass
chlorine is a poorer leaving group in aliphatic compounds
the C-Cl bond has partial double bond character and carbon is sp2 hybridised
questions.explanation: Resonance with the ring and the sp2 carbon make the C-Cl bond shorter and stronger and hard to break.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Drinking methanol is dangerous because in the body it is oxidised to
options: methanal, which damages the optic nerve
carbon dioxide only, which is harmless
questions.explanation: Methanol is oxidised to methanal and then methanoic acid, which can cause blindness and death.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Saytzeff's rule with an example.
questions.answer: In dehydrohalogenation or dehydration the preferred product is the more substituted (more stable) alkene. For example, 2-bromobutane with alcoholic KOH gives mainly but-2-ene rather than but-1-ene.
keyPoints: More substituted alkene is the major product
Hydrogen removed from the carbon with fewer hydrogens
questions.explanation: The more highly substituted double bond is more stable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are tertiary alcohols dehydrated more easily than primary alcohols?
questions.answer: Dehydration in acid proceeds through a carbocation intermediate. A tertiary carbocation is stabilised by three alkyl groups through inductive effect and hyperconjugation, so it forms more easily and the reaction is faster than for primary alcohols.
questions.explanation: The order of ease of dehydration is tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH3COOH is
questions.explanation: Two carbon atoms with a -COOH group give ethanoic acid (acetic acid).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and slow healing.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which compound undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?
questions.explanation: Cannizzaro reaction occurs in aldehydes with no alpha-hydrogen, such as benzaldehyde and methanal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The sugar present in DNA is
questions.explanation: DNA contains 2-deoxyribose, whereas RNA contains ribose.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanamide is treated with bromine and sodium hydroxide (Hoffmann bromamide degradation). The product is
questions.explanation: The reaction converts an amide into a primary amine with one carbon atom fewer, so CH3CONH2 gives CH3NH2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: At its isoelectric point, an amino acid in solution
options: has zero net charge and exists as a zwitterion
questions.explanation: At the isoelectric pH the positive and negative charges balance, so the molecule has no net charge and does not migrate in an electric field.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid and name the product.
questions.answer: CH3COOH + C2H5OH gives CH3COOC2H5 + H2O in the presence of concentrated H2SO4. The product is ethyl ethanoate (an ester), and the reaction is called esterification.
keyPoints: Acid plus alcohol with conc. H2SO4
questions.explanation: The reaction is reversible and the acid catalyst also removes water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What happens to a protein on denaturation? Give an everyday example.
questions.answer: Denaturation destroys the secondary and tertiary structures of a protein (and often its biological activity) through heat, acid or other agents, while the primary structure with its peptide bonds remains. Boiling an egg turns the soluble albumin into an insoluble white solid.
keyPoints: Secondary and tertiary structures are lost
Example such as boiling an egg or curdling of milk
questions.explanation: Loss of the three-dimensional shape leads to loss of function, for example in enzymes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a flower, pollen grains are produced in the
questions.explanation: The anther of the stamen contains pollen sacs where pollen grains develop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which hormone is secreted by the corpus luteum?
questions.explanation: After ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human sperm?
questions.explanation: Gametes are haploid, so a human sperm has 23 chromosomes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Male honey bees (drones) develop from unfertilised eggs. This type of reproduction is called
questions.explanation: Development of an egg into a new individual without fertilisation is parthenogenesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Menstruation occurs in the absence of pregnancy because
options: the level of FSH becomes very high
the ovum divides and is released
the corpus luteum degenerates and progesterone level falls, so the endometrium breaks down
questions.explanation: Without a signal from an embryo the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and the uterine lining is shed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which feature is typical of a wind-pollinated flower?
options: light, non-sticky pollen and a feathery stigma
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers produce large amounts of light pollen and have feathery stigmas to catch pollen from the air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is in vitro fertilisation (IVF)?
questions.answer: In vitro fertilisation is a technique in which an ovum and sperm are fused outside the body in a laboratory medium. The early embryo is then transferred to the uterus (or fallopian tube) to complete development, as in the test-tube baby programme.
keyPoints: Embryo is later transferred into the female
questions.explanation: It helps couples who cannot conceive naturally.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two devices that flowering plants use to prevent self-pollination and explain how each works.
questions.answer: In dichogamy, pollen release and stigma receptivity occur at different times. In herkogamy, the anther and stigma are placed so that pollen cannot reach the stigma of the same flower. Self-incompatibility, where pollen of the same plant fails to germinate, is another device.
keyPoints: Herkogamy: spatial separation of anther and stigma
questions.explanation: Cross-pollination increases genetic variation among offspring.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA has uracil in place of thymine.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: In humans, the sex of the child is determined by
questions.explanation: All eggs carry an X chromosome, whereas a sperm carries either X (girl) or Y (boy).

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Mendel's law of segregation states that
options: the two alleles of a gene separate so that each gamete receives only one
genes of different traits always remain linked
questions.explanation: Allele pairs separate during gamete formation, so each gamete carries one allele of each gene.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: The phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a Mendelian dihybrid cross is
questions.explanation: AaBb × AaBb gives 9 double dominant : 3 : 3 : 1 double recessive.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Two pink-flowered snapdragon plants (incomplete dominance) are crossed. The ratio of red : pink : white offspring is expected to be
questions.explanation: RW × RW gives RR : RW : WW = 1 : 2 : 1, and the phenotypes match the genotypes in incomplete dominance.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: A colour-blind man (X-linked recessive) marries a normal woman who is not a carrier. Their sons will be
questions.explanation: Sons receive the Y chromosome from the father and an X from the normal mother, so none inherit colour blindness.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: What is transcription? Name the enzyme that carries it out.
questions.answer: Transcription is the process in which one strand of DNA is used as a template to make a complementary RNA molecule. The enzyme RNA polymerase carries it out.
keyPoints: Complementary base pairing, U in place of T
questions.explanation: Transcription is the first step in the flow of information from DNA to protein.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The forelimbs of a human, bat and whale have the same bone plan but different functions. What do these structures show about evolution?
questions.answer: They are homologous organs showing divergent evolution. The common structural plan suggests a common ancestor, while adaptation to different modes of life, such as grasping, flying and swimming, produced the differences in form.
questions.explanation: In contrast, analogous organs like bird and insect wings have similar function but different origins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of in situ conservation?
questions.explanation: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat, as in national parks, sanctuaries and sacred groves.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The first recombinant human insulin was produced using
questions.explanation: The human insulin genes for the A and B chains were introduced into E. coli, which made the chains that were then joined.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) is caused by deficiency of the enzyme
questions.explanation: ADA deficiency cripples the immune system and was the first disorder treated by gene therapy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The main cause of depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer is
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere which catalytically destroy ozone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organisms are the first to colonise a bare rock in primary ecological succession?
questions.explanation: Lichens secrete acids that weather rock and form the first soil, preparing the way for mosses and later plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: DDT sprayed in a water body shows the highest concentration in the tissues of
questions.explanation: DDT is not broken down and accumulates at each trophic level, a process called biomagnification, reaching its highest level in top carnivores.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the three steps of one cycle of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
questions.answer: The three steps are denaturation (heating to separate the DNA strands), annealing (primers bind to the template at a lower temperature) and extension (Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to make new strands).
questions.explanation: Repeated cycles amplify the target DNA exponentially.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State any three causes of loss of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Major causes are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation of species by hunting or harvesting, introduction of alien species that outcompete native ones, and co-extinction when a dependent species disappears with its host.
questions.explanation: Habitat destruction is regarded as the most important cause.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: In SI units, the value of 1/(4 pi epsilon_0) is approximately
questions.explanation: The Coulomb constant k = 1/(4 pi epsilon_0) is about 9 × 10^9 N m^2 C^-2; 8.85 × 10^-12 is epsilon_0 itself.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Which of the following materials is a good electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber has almost no free electrons; the metals listed are good conductors.

questions.q: Charges of +4 microcoulomb and +1 microcoulomb are 0.3 m apart. At what distance from the +4 microcoulomb charge, on the line joining them, is the net electric field zero?
questions.explanation: Setting 4/x^2 = 1/(0.3 - x)^2 gives 2(0.3 - x) = x, so x = 0.2 m.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: State the principle of superposition for the electrostatic force on a charge due to several other charges.
questions.answer: The net force on a charge due to a number of other charges is the vector sum of the forces that each of them exerts on it individually, as if the others were absent.
keyPoints: Forces from each charge act independently
Net force is the vector sum
Applies to fields and potentials as well
questions.explanation: The force between any two charges is not affected by the presence of other charges.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab is then inserted between the plates. How do the potential difference and stored energy change?
questions.answer: The charge stays constant while the capacitance rises by the factor K. Since V = Q/C, the potential difference falls to V/K, and U = Q^2/(2C) also falls to U/K. The energy is used in pulling the slab into the gap.
keyPoints: V and U both decrease by the factor K
questions.explanation: In contrast, with the battery connected the voltage is fixed and the energy increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A galvanometer is an instrument used to
options: detect or measure small electric currents
questions.explanation: A moving-coil galvanometer detects small currents through the deflection of its coil.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule relates current, field and force on a conductor; the right-hand rule is used for induced current.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Why is a potentiometer preferred over a voltmeter for measuring the emf of a cell?
options: it draws no current from the cell at the balance point
it has a very low resistance
questions.explanation: At balance no current flows through the cell, so its terminal voltage equals its emf, whereas a voltmeter draws some current.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long ideal solenoid with 1000 turns per metre carrying 2 A is about (mu_0 = 4 pi × 10^-7 T m/A)
questions.explanation: B = mu_0 n I = 4 pi × 10^-7 × 1000 × 2, which is about 2.5 × 10^-3 T.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Define drift velocity and write the relation between current and drift velocity.
questions.answer: Drift velocity is the average velocity with which free electrons move in a conductor under an applied electric field. The current is I = n e A v_d, where n is the number of free electrons per unit volume and A is the cross-sectional area.
keyPoints: Average velocity of electrons under a field
n is electron density and A is the area
questions.explanation: Drift velocity is very small, of the order of millimetres per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Distinguish between diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials on the basis of their behaviour in an external magnetic field.
questions.answer: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnetic field and have relative permeability slightly below 1. Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted and are magnetised along the field. Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted and can be permanently magnetised.
questions.explanation: Examples are bismuth, aluminium and iron respectively.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following devices works on the principle of electromagnetic induction?
questions.explanation: A transformer relies on a changing flux in one coil inducing an emf in another.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The power factor of a purely resistive AC circuit is
questions.explanation: Voltage and current are in phase, so cos(phi) = cos 0 = 1.

questions.subject: science

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The current through a 0.5 H coil falls uniformly from 2 A to zero in 0.1 s. The magnitude of the self-induced emf is
questions.explanation: emf = L (change in I)/t = 0.5 × 2/0.1 = 10 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: At resonance in a series LCR circuit, the current in the circuit is
questions.explanation: At resonance X_L = X_C, impedance is minimum and equals R, so the current is maximum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a rotating-coil AC generator, the induced emf is maximum when the plane of the coil is
options: at 45 degrees to the field only
questions.explanation: When the plane is parallel to the field, the flux is zero but changing at the greatest rate, so the emf is maximum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is meant by wattless current?
questions.answer: The current in an AC circuit that does no net work, in a purely inductive or capacitive circuit where the phase difference between voltage and current is 90 degrees, is called wattless current. The average power consumed is zero.
keyPoints: Occurs in pure inductor or capacitor
questions.explanation: Power = V_rms I_rms cos(phi) and cos 90 degrees = 0.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does an induction cooker heat a metal vessel without a flame or a hot plate?
questions.answer: A coil below the surface carries a rapidly alternating current and produces a rapidly changing magnetic field. This induces large eddy currents in the base of the metal vessel, and the current heats the vessel through its resistance.
keyPoints: Alternating current in a coil gives a changing field
Eddy currents are induced in the vessel
questions.explanation: The cooktop itself stays comparatively cool because it is not a conductor of the induced currents.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which mirror can form both real and virtual images of a real object?
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms real images for objects beyond the focus and a virtual image for objects within the focus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately
questions.explanation: c is about 3 × 10^8 m/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 15 cm from it. The image distance is
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm (real image, magnification 2).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A medium has refractive index root 2 with respect to air. The critical angle for light going from the medium to air is
questions.explanation: sin C = 1/n = 1/root 2, so C = 45 degrees.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, lambda = 600 nm, slit separation = 0.3 mm and screen distance = 1.5 m. The fringe width is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Light is reflected from glass of refractive index root 3. At what angle of incidence is the reflected light completely plane polarised?
questions.explanation: By Brewster's law tan i_B = n = root 3, so i_B = 60 degrees.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Huygens' principle.
questions.answer: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out with the speed of light in that medium. The new wavefront at a later time is the surface that touches all these wavelets in the forward direction.
keyPoints: Each point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets
Wavelets travel with the speed of the wave
New wavefront is the forward envelope
questions.explanation: It explains reflection and refraction using the wave picture.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do astronomical telescopes use objective lenses or mirrors of large diameter?
questions.answer: A large aperture collects more light, so faint distant objects look brighter. It also improves the resolving power, because the limit of resolution is about 1.22 lambda/D, so a larger D lets the telescope separate closer objects.
questions.explanation: Diffraction at the aperture limits how fine the detail can be.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The neutron was discovered by
questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: The Balmer series of the hydrogen spectrum lies mainly in the
questions.explanation: Balmer lines arise from transitions to n = 2 and four of them are visible.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A metal has a work function of 2.48 eV. Using hc = 1240 eV nm, its threshold wavelength is
questions.explanation: lambda_0 = hc/phi = 1240/2.48 = 500 nm.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The nuclear radius varies as R = R0 A^(1/3). The ratio of the radii of nuclei with mass numbers 8 and 27 is
questions.explanation: R is proportional to the cube root of A, so the ratio is 2 : 3.
