questions.explanation: K' = 2hf - phi = 2K + phi, which is greater than 2K.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: State any two postulates of Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom.
questions.answer: An electron revolves in certain stable circular orbits without radiating energy, and in these orbits its angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2 pi. Radiation is emitted or absorbed only when the electron jumps between orbits, with photon energy hf equal to the difference in energy of the orbits.
keyPoints: Photon emitted or absorbed during a jump, hf = E2 - E1
questions.explanation: These postulates explain the discrete line spectrum of hydrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: What are the roles of the moderator and the control rods in a nuclear reactor?
questions.answer: The moderator, such as heavy water or graphite, slows down fast neutrons so that they can cause further fission of uranium-235. Control rods of cadmium or boron absorb neutrons to keep the chain reaction steady and can shut the reactor down.
questions.explanation: Without control the number of fissions would grow exponentially.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The law that relates the solubility of a gas in a liquid to the pressure of the gas is
questions.explanation: Henry's law says that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to its partial pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of conductivity of an electrolytic solution is
questions.explanation: Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity, so it has units of siemens per metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The van't Hoff factor for a completely dissociated 0.1 M NaCl solution is
questions.explanation: Each formula unit gives two particles, Na+ and Cl-, so i = 2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The molal depression constant for water is 1.86 K kg/mol. The freezing point of water falls by how much when 0.5 mol of glucose is dissolved in 1 kg of water?
questions.explanation: Depression = Kf × m = 1.86 × 0.5 = 0.93 K.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: For a cell with E°cell = 1.10 V and n = 2, the standard free energy change is about (F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Delta G = -nFE = -2 × 96500 × 1.10 = -212 300 J, about -212 kJ/mol; negative means spontaneous.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Given limiting molar conductivities in S cm^2 mol^-1 of HCl = 426, NaCl = 126 and CH3COONa = 91, the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid is
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law, Lambda(CH3COOH) = 426 + 91 - 126 = 391 S cm^2 mol^-1.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions.
questions.answer: At infinite dilution the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte equals the sum of the limiting molar conductivities of its cation and anion, each ion contributing independently irrespective of the other ion present.
keyPoints: Sum of contributions of cation and anion
questions.explanation: It is used to find the limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolytes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the function of a salt bridge in a galvanic cell?
questions.answer: The salt bridge completes the electrical circuit by letting ions move between the two half-cells, and it keeps each solution electrically neutral as charge builds up. It also minimises the liquid junction potential. Without it the cell would stop working quickly.
questions.explanation: A salt bridge usually contains an inert electrolyte such as KCl or KNO3.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a new pathway with lower activation energy but is not consumed and does not change the overall enthalpy.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In the lanthanoid series, electrons are successively added to the
questions.explanation: The lanthanoids (Ce to Lu) are the 4f series.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 20 minutes. The fraction of the reactant left after 60 minutes is
questions.explanation: 60 minutes is three half-lives, so (1/2)^3 = 1/8 remains.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In acidic solution, permanganate ion (MnO4-) is reduced to
questions.explanation: In acid medium MnO4- accepts five electrons and forms the nearly colourless Mn2+.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: For a first-order reaction, which graph is a straight line with slope equal to -k?
questions.explanation: Integrating the rate law gives ln[A] = ln[A]0 - kt, a straight line when ln[A] is plotted against time.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Zinc is not regarded as a typical transition element because
options: it does not form any compounds
it has no d electrons at all
it has a completely filled d subshell in its atom and in its common ion
questions.explanation: Zn has the 3d10 configuration in the atom and in Zn2+, so it lacks the partly filled d orbitals that define transition-metal behaviour.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: What are interstitial compounds? State two properties.
questions.answer: Interstitial compounds are formed when small atoms such as hydrogen, carbon or nitrogen occupy the voids in the crystal lattice of a transition metal. They are generally very hard, have high melting points and keep metallic conductivity, but are chemically inert.
keyPoints: Small atoms trapped in lattice voids
questions.explanation: Steel and metal hydrides are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Why do the actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states than the lanthanoids?
questions.answer: The 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals in actinoids are of comparable energy, so electrons from all of them can take part in bonding. In lanthanoids the 4f electrons are tightly held, so the +3 state dominates.
keyPoints: 4f electrons in lanthanoids are held more tightly
questions.explanation: 5f orbitals extend further out than 4f orbitals and are less shielded by the other electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The central metal atom in vitamin B12 is
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) is a cobalt complex; haemoglobin contains iron and chlorophyll magnesium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the ligand NH3, the donor atom that bonds to the metal is
questions.explanation: The lone pair on the nitrogen atom is donated to the metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Excess silver nitrate solution is added to one mole of [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2. How many moles of AgCl precipitate?
questions.explanation: Only the two chloride ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate; the Cl inside the bracket is firmly bound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The hybridisation of cobalt in the inner orbital complex [Co(NH3)6]3+ is
questions.explanation: Strong-field NH3 pairs the 3d electrons of Co3+, freeing two 3d orbitals for d2sp3 hybridisation in an octahedral complex.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is an ambidentate ligand that can show linkage isomerism?
questions.explanation: NO2- can bind through nitrogen (nitro) or oxygen (nitrito), so it is ambidentate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The compound [Pt(NH3)4Cl2]Cl2 is dissolved in water. The total number of ions per formula unit in solution is
questions.explanation: It gives one complex cation [Pt(NH3)4Cl2]2+ and two Cl- ions, three ions in all.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Mention two applications of coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Coordination compounds are used in biology (haemoglobin contains iron, chlorophyll contains magnesium), in medicine (cisplatin as an anticancer drug and EDTA for removing toxic metals), in metallurgy such as extraction of silver and gold as cyanide complexes, and in analysis such as hardness estimation with EDTA.
keyPoints: Medicine such as cisplatin or chelation therapy
Extraction of metals or analytical tests
questions.explanation: Complex formation changes the solubility and reactivity of metal ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Most copper(I) compounds are colourless, whereas copper(II) compounds are usually coloured. Explain.
questions.answer: Cu+ has the configuration 3d10, so all d orbitals are full and no d-d transition is possible, making it colourless. Cu2+ has 3d9 with one unpaired electron which can be excited between split d levels by absorbing visible light, giving colour.
keyPoints: Cu+ is d10, no d-d transitions
Cu2+ is d9 with a vacancy
Absorption of visible light gives colour
questions.explanation: Colour in transition-metal complexes arises from d-d electronic transitions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of chloroform is
questions.explanation: Chloroform is trichloromethane, CHCl3.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
questions.explanation: In propan-2-ol the carbon bearing -OH is attached to two other carbon atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: 2C2H5OH + 2Na gives 2C2H5ONa + H2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanol on oxidation with excess acidified potassium dichromate gives
questions.explanation: Strong oxidising agents oxidise a primary alcohol through the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Phenol on heating with chloroform and aqueous sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification, mainly gives
questions.explanation: This is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, which introduces a -CHO group at the ortho position to give 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Thionyl chloride is the preferred reagent for converting an alcohol into an alkyl chloride because
options: the by-products SO2 and HCl are gases and escape, leaving a pure product
questions.explanation: ROH + SOCl2 gives RCl + SO2 + HCl, so no separation of by-products from the alkyl halide is needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name a simple chemical test to distinguish phenol from ethanol.
questions.answer: Add neutral ferric chloride solution. Phenol gives a violet colouration, while ethanol gives no colour.
questions.explanation: The colour is due to formation of an iron(III)-phenoxide complex.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Haloalkanes are polar, yet they are only slightly soluble in water. Why?
questions.answer: To dissolve, a haloalkane must break the strong hydrogen bonds between water molecules, but the new attractions between haloalkane and water molecules are weaker. The energy released is not enough to compensate, so solubility is low.
questions.explanation: Haloalkanes dissolve readily in organic solvents instead.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH3COCH3 is
questions.explanation: A three-carbon ketone is called propanone (acetone).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Most enzymes are chemically
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts, and nearly all are globular proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanal, on treatment with dilute NaOH, forms
questions.explanation: This is the aldol reaction, in which two molecules of ethanal combine to give 3-hydroxybutanal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The carbylamine reaction is a test for
questions.explanation: Primary amines on heating with chloroform and alcoholic KOH give foul-smelling isocyanides.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in the open-chain structure of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose is an aldohexose; carbons 2, 3, 4 and 5 each carry four different groups.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which compound has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid forms strong hydrogen-bonded dimers; its boiling point (about 118 degrees C) is above that of propan-1-ol (about 97 degrees C), propanal and butane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two differences between DNA and RNA.
questions.answer: DNA contains deoxyribose sugar and the base thymine and is usually double-stranded, while RNA contains ribose sugar and the base uracil and is usually single-stranded.
keyPoints: Deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA
Thymine in DNA, uracil in RNA
questions.explanation: Both are polymers of nucleotides joined by phosphodiester bonds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic addition?
questions.answer: An aldehyde carbonyl carbon has only one alkyl group, so it is less hindered and more positively charged. In a ketone, two electron-releasing alkyl groups reduce the positive charge on carbon and make the approach of the nucleophile more crowded.
keyPoints: One alkyl group gives less electron donation
questions.explanation: Both steric and electronic effects favour aldehydes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The hormone mainly responsible for the development of male secondary sexual characters is
questions.explanation: Testosterone, secreted by the Leydig cells, controls male secondary sexual characters.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In humans, the embryo gets implanted in the
questions.explanation: The blastocyst embeds in the endometrium of the uterus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A typical angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) at maturity has
questions.explanation: It consists of the egg apparatus (3 cells), 3 antipodals and a large central cell with two polar nuclei, giving 7 cells and 8 nuclei.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which structure connects the foetus to the placenta?
questions.explanation: The umbilical cord carries blood between the foetus and the placenta.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The copper-T used for contraception acts mainly because
options: it permanently blocks the fallopian tubes
it kills the ovum in the ovary
copper ions released in the uterus suppress sperm motility and fertilising ability
questions.explanation: Copper ions reduce sperm movement and fertilising capacity and the device also makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Suppose gametes were produced by mitosis instead of meiosis. What would happen to the chromosome number in successive generations?
options: it would vary randomly but stay the same on average
questions.explanation: Fertilisation joins two diploid gametes, doubling the chromosome number each generation; meiosis prevents this by halving it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the three main stages of sexual reproduction in organisms.
questions.answer: The stages are the pre-fertilisation events (gametogenesis and gamete transfer), fertilisation (fusion of gametes to form the zygote) and post-fertilisation events (embryo development).
questions.explanation: In plants post-fertilisation events include formation of seed and fruit.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the function of the tapetum in an anther.
questions.answer: The tapetum is the innermost layer of the anther wall. It nourishes the developing pollen grains and supplies materials for the formation of their outer wall, and its cells are rich in nutrients and enzymes.
keyPoints: Innermost layer of the anther wall
questions.explanation: Defective tapetum often leads to male sterility.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The basic unit of heredity that controls a trait is the
questions.explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a functional product and controls a trait.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by
questions.explanation: Darwin (with Wallace) proposed that nature selects individuals best adapted to the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: A test cross between a heterozygous tall plant (Tt) and a dwarf plant (tt) gives tall and dwarf offspring in the ratio
questions.explanation: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Down syndrome is caused by
options: a point mutation in the beta-globin gene
questions.explanation: Trisomy 21 gives 47 chromosomes in the cells of a person with Down syndrome.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Sickle-cell anaemia results from a point mutation that changes
options: glutamic acid to valine in the beta chain of haemoglobin
valine to glutamic acid in the beta chain
an alpha chain to a gamma chain
questions.explanation: A single base change (GAG to GUG in the mRNA) substitutes valine for glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta chain.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: In the Hershey-Chase experiment, bacteriophage DNA was labelled with
questions.explanation: DNA contains phosphorus but no sulphur, whereas protein contains sulphur; infected cells received 32P, proving DNA is the genetic material.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: State two characteristics of the genetic code.
questions.answer: The code is triplet (three bases code for one amino acid), degenerate (more than one codon for most amino acids), non-overlapping, comma-free and nearly universal across organisms.
questions.explanation: There are 64 codons, 61 of which code for amino acids and 3 are stop codons.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: How can the degeneracy of the genetic code protect an organism from the effects of some mutations?
questions.answer: Because several codons code for the same amino acid, a change in the third base of a codon often still specifies the same amino acid. Such silent mutations leave the protein unchanged, so harm is avoided.
questions.explanation: Mutations in the first or second base are more likely to change the amino acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a biofertiliser?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes and acts as a biofertiliser.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Methane, like carbon dioxide, absorbs infrared radiation and warms the atmosphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A lichen is an example of
options: mutualism between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium
questions.explanation: The fungus gets food from the photosynthetic partner, which gets protection and water in return.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Golden rice has been genetically modified to be rich in
questions.explanation: It contains genes for beta-carotene synthesis, which the body converts to vitamin A.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In logistic population growth, as the population size approaches the carrying capacity K, the growth rate
questions.explanation: Limited resources slow down growth, giving an S-shaped curve that levels off at K.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Species diversity is generally higher in tropical regions than in temperate regions mainly because tropical environments
options: are more stable, receive more solar energy and have had a longer evolutionary time
questions.explanation: Tropical climates have been relatively undisturbed for long periods, are less seasonal and have high productivity, allowing more species to evolve.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is bioremediation? Give an example.
questions.answer: Bioremediation is the use of living organisms, mainly microbes or plants, to clean up polluted soil or water by breaking down or removing pollutants. An example is the use of bacteria to degrade oil spills.
keyPoints: Use of organisms to remove pollutants
questions.explanation: It is generally cheaper and less harmful than chemical cleaning.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between the grazing food chain and the detritus food chain.
questions.answer: A grazing food chain begins with green plants (producers) and passes energy to herbivores and then carnivores. A detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter that is eaten by decomposers and detritivores, and then passes to their predators. In many ecosystems the detritus chain carries more energy than the grazing chain.
keyPoints: Detritus chain starts with dead organic matter
Decomposers are key in detritus chain
questions.explanation: Both chains are connected in a food web.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Quantisation of electric charge means that the charge on any body is
options: any real number multiple of e
questions.explanation: Charge exists only in whole-number multiples of the elementary charge e, so q = ne.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct unit of electric field?
questions.explanation: Electric field is force per unit charge (N/C), which is equivalent to V/m.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Capacitors of 2 microfarad and 4 microfarad are connected in parallel. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: In parallel the capacitances add: 2 + 4 = 6 microfarad.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A point charge q is placed at the centre of a cube. The electric flux through one face of the cube is
questions.explanation: The total flux q/epsilon_0 is shared equally among the six identical faces.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Charges of +2 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb are 0.1 m apart. The electrostatic potential energy of this pair is (k = 9 × 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)
questions.explanation: U = k q1 q2 / r = 9 × 10^9 × (-4 × 10^-12)/0.1 = -0.36 J; the negative sign shows the charges attract.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Why can two electric field lines never cross each other?
questions.answer: The tangent to a field line at a point gives the direction of the electric field there. If two lines crossed, the field at the crossing point would have two directions at once, which is impossible, so field lines never intersect.
keyPoints: Crossing would mean two directions at one point
Field has a unique direction at every point
questions.explanation: The same logic applies to lines of force in any vector field.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Why is it relatively safe to stay inside a closed metal car during a lightning storm?
questions.answer: The metal body acts as a conducting shell. The charge from lightning spreads over the outer surface and the electric field inside a hollow conductor is zero, so the passengers inside are shielded from the discharge.
keyPoints: Car body acts as a hollow conductor
Charge stays on the outer surface
questions.explanation: This principle is also used in Faraday cages.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Which material is used as the core of an electromagnet?
questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, which suits electromagnets.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Two resistors of 3 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series. Their equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 3 + 5 = 8 ohm.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A steady current of 0.5 A flows in a wire for 10 minutes. The charge that passes through the wire is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: An electron moves at 2 × 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. The magnetic force on it is (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with P = 10 ohm, Q = 20 ohm and R = 30 ohm, where P/Q = R/S. The value of S is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: When the temperature of a semiconductor is raised, its resistance
questions.explanation: More charge carriers are released at higher temperature, so the resistance of a semiconductor falls, unlike that of a metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: State the Biot-Savart law.
questions.answer: The magnetic field dB produced at a point by a small current element I dl is directly proportional to the current, the length of the element and the sine of the angle between dl and the line to the point, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance, dB = (mu_0/4 pi) I dl sin(theta)/r^2.
keyPoints: dB proportional to I dl sin(theta)
questions.explanation: It is used to find the field of loops and other current distributions.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A current loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field. Why does it rotate but not move as a whole?
questions.answer: The forces on opposite sides of the loop are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero and there is no translation. These forces are not along the same line, so they form a couple that exerts a torque tau = m B sin(theta) and rotates the loop.
questions.explanation: This is the principle of the moving-coil galvanometer and the electric motor.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday (and independently Joseph Henry) discovered electromagnetic induction in the 1830s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is
questions.explanation: Flux = B × A, and one weber equals one tesla metre squared.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A loop of area 0.2 m^2 is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T with the field making an angle of 60 degrees with the normal to the loop. The magnetic flux is
questions.explanation: Flux = B A cos(60 degrees) = 0.5 × 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.05 Wb.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 5 A. Its rms value is about

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An ideal step-up transformer has a turns ratio of 1 : 10. If the primary current is 10 A, the secondary current is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer V_p I_p = V_s I_s; the voltage is raised 10 times, so the current falls to one tenth, 1 A.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A metal rod 0.5 m long moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T, with its length perpendicular to both. The motional emf across its ends is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between self-induction and mutual induction.
questions.answer: In self-induction a changing current in a coil induces an emf in the same coil. In mutual induction a changing current in one coil induces an emf in a neighbouring coil. The emf is characterised by the self-inductance L or the mutual inductance M, both measured in henry.
questions.explanation: Transformers use mutual induction; chokes use self-induction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bulb connected in series with a coil with iron core glows dimly when connected to an AC source, but brightly when connected to a DC source of the same voltage. Explain.
questions.answer: With AC the inductor offers reactance X_L = 2 pi f L in addition to resistance, so the impedance is high and the current is small. With DC there is no change in current once steady, so there is no back emf and only the small resistance of the coil limits the current.
questions.explanation: An inductor passes DC easily but opposes AC, and more so at higher frequency.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour is deviated the most?
questions.explanation: Violet has the highest refractive index in glass and therefore bends the most.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The focal length of a plane mirror is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror is a surface of infinite radius of curvature, so f = infinity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. The image is formed at
options: 15 cm in front of the mirror
60 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/30 + 1/30 = 1/15, so v = +15 cm, a virtual image behind the mirror.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two thin lenses of powers +10 D and -2 D are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: Total power = 10 - 2 = 8 D, so f = 1/8 m = 12.5 cm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A prism of angle 60 degrees has refractive index root 2. The angle of minimum deviation is
questions.explanation: n = sin((A + D)/2)/sin(A/2) gives sin((A + D)/2) = root 2 × 0.5 = 0.707, so (A + D)/2 = 45 degrees and D = 30 degrees.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two ordinary bulbs shone on a screen do not produce a stable interference pattern because
options: the bulbs have different powers only
the light from them is not coherent
questions.explanation: Independent sources emit with rapidly and randomly changing phase differences, so the pattern keeps shifting and averages out.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between a real image and a virtual image.
questions.answer: A real image is formed when light rays actually meet at a point; it can be obtained on a screen and is inverted for a single mirror or lens. A virtual image is formed when rays only appear to diverge from a point; it cannot be taken on a screen and is erect.
keyPoints: Real: rays actually meet, can be projected
Virtual: rays appear to come from a point, cannot be projected
Real is usually inverted, virtual erect
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms virtual images.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is blue light preferred to red light when a microscope is used to see very fine detail?
questions.answer: The limit of resolution is proportional to the wavelength of light used. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red, so it can resolve objects that are closer together and gives a sharper view of fine detail.
keyPoints: Resolution limit is proportional to wavelength
Blue wavelength is shorter than red
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes use even smaller de Broglie wavelengths.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The SI unit of radioactivity is
questions.explanation: One becquerel is one decay per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Which radiation from radioactive substances has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy photons with no charge and penetrate matter the most.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: In beta-minus decay of a nucleus, the atomic number
options: increases by 1 and the mass number is unchanged
decreases by 1 and the mass number is unchanged
decreases by 2 and the mass number decreases by 4
is unchanged and the mass number increases by 1
questions.explanation: A neutron changes into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino, so Z rises by 1 and A stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Photoelectrons from a surface have a maximum kinetic energy of 3 eV. The stopping potential is
questions.explanation: eV_0 = K_max, so V_0 = 3 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Using E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV, the energy of the photon emitted in the transition n = 3 to n = 2 in hydrogen is about

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Nuclear density is nearly the same for all nuclei because
options: nuclear volume is proportional to the mass number
nuclear radius is independent of mass number
questions.explanation: R is proportional to A^(1/3), so volume is proportional to A, and mass is also proportional to A, making density constant.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: What is radioactivity?
questions.answer: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation, such as alpha particles, beta particles or gamma rays, from the nuclei of unstable atoms as they change into more stable nuclei.
keyPoints: Emission of alpha, beta or gamma radiation
questions.explanation: It was discovered by Henri Becquerel.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Compare nuclear fission and nuclear fusion in two points.
questions.answer: In fission a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 splits into two lighter nuclei after absorbing a neutron, releasing energy and more neutrons. In fusion two light nuclei such as hydrogen isotopes combine to form a heavier nucleus and release energy, but it needs a very high temperature to overcome the Coulomb repulsion.
questions.explanation: Fusion is the source of the Sun's energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following solutions does not conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a non-electrolyte and does not produce ions in solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The value of one faraday is approximately
questions.explanation: One faraday is the charge of one mole of electrons, about 96 500 C.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: 10 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 90 g of water. The mass percentage of NaCl in the solution is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The vapour pressure of pure liquid A is 100 mm Hg. In an ideal solution where the mole fraction of A is 0.6, the partial vapour pressure of A is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law p_A = x_A p_A^0 = 0.6 × 100 = 60 mm Hg.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The osmotic pressure of a 0.01 M solution of a non-electrolyte at 300 K is (R = 0.0821 L atm mol^-1 K^-1)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride with inert electrodes, the gas liberated at the cathode is
questions.explanation: Water is reduced more easily than Na+, so H2 forms at the cathode, Cl2 at the anode and NaOH is left in solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are azeotropes?
questions.answer: Azeotropes are liquid mixtures that boil at a constant temperature and distil over with the same composition as the liquid, so they cannot be separated by simple fractional distillation. Ethanol-water mixture at about 95 per cent ethanol is an example.
keyPoints: Vapour has same composition as liquid
Cannot be separated by fractional distillation
questions.explanation: They form from non-ideal solutions showing large deviations from Raoult's law.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does zinc-coated (galvanised) iron resist rusting even when the zinc coating is scratched?
questions.answer: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so in the presence of moisture it is oxidised in preference to iron and acts as a sacrificial anode. The exposed iron acts as the cathode and is protected from corrosion until the zinc is used up.
keyPoints: Zinc is more reactive than iron
questions.explanation: Tin coating, in contrast, only protects while the surface is intact.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The unit of the rate of a chemical reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate is the change in concentration per unit time.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Which transition metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury has a melting point of about -39 degrees C because of its filled d subshell and weak metallic bonding.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0231 min^-1. The half-life is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of an ion with three unpaired electrons is about
questions.explanation: mu = root(n(n + 2)) = root 15, which is about 3.87 BM.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In an Arrhenius plot of ln k against 1/T, the slope of the straight line is
questions.explanation: ln k = ln A - Ea/(RT), so the slope is -Ea/R.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Mn2+ is very difficult to oxidise to Mn3+ mainly because
options: Mn2+ has a half-filled 3d5 configuration which is particularly stable
Mn2+ has a completely filled 3d subshell
Mn3+ is smaller than a proton
questions.explanation: The d5 configuration of Mn2+ has extra stability due to exchange energy, whereas Fe2+ (d6) oxidises easily to the d5 Fe3+ ion.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: What is a pseudo first-order reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: It is a reaction that is actually of higher order but behaves as first order because one reactant is present in such large excess that its concentration is practically constant. Hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate in excess water or the inversion of cane sugar are examples.
keyPoints: Higher order reaction behaving as first order
Example: hydrolysis of ester or inversion of sucrose
questions.explanation: The constant concentration of water is absorbed into the rate constant.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Write the balanced ionic equation for the oxidation of ferrous ions by permanganate in acidic medium.
questions.answer: 5Fe2+ + MnO4- + 8H+ gives 5Fe3+ + Mn2+ + 4H2O. Each Fe2+ loses one electron and each permanganate ion accepts five electrons.
questions.explanation: The decolourisation of the purple permanganate marks the end point of the titration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a neutral ligand?
questions.explanation: Water is an uncharged molecule that donates a lone pair of electrons through oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The anticancer drug cisplatin is a coordination complex of
questions.explanation: Cisplatin is cis-[Pt(NH3)2Cl2].

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many ions are produced per formula unit when [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissolves in water?
questions.explanation: It gives one [Co(NH3)6]3+ ion and three Cl- ions, four ions in all.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex ion [Cu(NH3)4]2+ is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named first (tetraammine) followed by the metal with its oxidation state, copper(II) here.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in an octahedral high-spin d4 complex?
questions.explanation: In a weak field the electrons occupy t2g^3 eg^1 with all four unpaired, while a strong field gives t2g^4 with two unpaired.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br and [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 are ionisation isomers. Which statement is correct?
options: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br gives a pale-yellow precipitate with silver nitrate
[Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 gives a pale-yellow precipitate with silver nitrate
both give a precipitate with barium chloride
questions.explanation: In [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br the bromide ion is outside the coordination sphere and precipitates as AgBr, while in the other isomer bromide is bound and sulphate is free.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define coordination number and coordination sphere with an example.
questions.answer: The coordination number is the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to the central metal ion. The coordination sphere is the central metal with the ligands attached to it, written in square brackets. In [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 the coordination number is 6 and the sphere is [Co(NH3)6]3+.
keyPoints: Number of donor atoms bonded to the metal
Coordination sphere is within square brackets
Example with Co and six NH3
questions.explanation: Counter ions outside the brackets are not part of the sphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are chelate complexes more stable than comparable complexes with monodentate ligands?
questions.answer: A polydentate ligand forms ring structures with the metal and, when it replaces several monodentate ligands, the number of free particles in solution increases. This raises the entropy and makes the complex more stable, which is called the chelate effect.
questions.explanation: For example [Ni(en)3]2+ is more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]2+.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The compound C6H5OH is called
questions.explanation: A hydroxyl group attached directly to a benzene ring gives phenol.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Among ethane, chloroethane, ethanol and dimethyl ether, which has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, giving it a boiling point of about 78 degrees C, higher than the others.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bromoethane reacts with aqueous KOH to give mainly
questions.explanation: Aqueous KOH brings about nucleophilic substitution (OH- replaces Br-), whereas alcoholic KOH causes elimination.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bromoethane heated with alcoholic KOH gives
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HBr in an elimination (dehydrohalogenation) reaction to give an alkene.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bromomethane is treated with sodium metal in dry ether (Wurtz reaction). The main organic product is
questions.explanation: 2CH3Br + 2Na gives CH3-CH3 + 2NaBr, joining two alkyl groups.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Propene undergoes hydroboration followed by oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. The main product is
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov alcohol, so the OH goes to the terminal carbon.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What happens when phenol is treated with sodium hydroxide? What does this show?
questions.answer: Phenol reacts with NaOH to form sodium phenoxide and water, C6H5OH + NaOH gives C6H5ONa + H2O. This shows that phenol is acidic, unlike alcohols which do not react with aqueous alkali.
keyPoints: Alcohols do not react with NaOH
questions.explanation: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is p-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol?
questions.answer: The nitro group is strongly electron-withdrawing through its -I and -M effects. It delocalises and stabilises the negative charge on the p-nitrophenoxide ion, so the ion forms more easily and the compound is a stronger acid.
keyPoints: Stabilises the phenoxide ion by delocalisation
More stable conjugate base means stronger acid
questions.explanation: Electron-releasing groups such as methyl have the opposite effect.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Proteins are polymers of
questions.explanation: Amino acids are linked by peptide bonds to make proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When an aldehyde is warmed with Fehling's solution, the precipitate formed is
questions.explanation: The copper(II) complex is reduced to red-brown copper(I) oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Reduction of propanone with sodium borohydride gives
questions.explanation: Ketones are reduced to secondary alcohols.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aniline reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate of
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group strongly activates the ortho and para positions, so all three are brominated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride on treatment with cuprous chloride gives
questions.explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction, in which the diazonium group is replaced by Cl, giving chlorobenzene with loss of nitrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: One strand of DNA has the base sequence 5'-ATGC-3'. The complementary strand reads
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G pairs with C, and the strands are antiparallel, so the partner reads 3'-TACG-5'.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are essential amino acids? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Essential amino acids are those that the human body cannot synthesise and must obtain from the diet. Examples are valine, leucine, lysine and isoleucine.
keyPoints: Cannot be synthesised by the body
Examples such as valine, leucine or lysine
questions.explanation: Non-essential amino acids, such as glycine and alanine, can be made in the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are carboxylic acids much more acidic than phenols?
questions.answer: On losing a proton, a carboxylate ion has its negative charge shared equally between two oxygen atoms by resonance, which stabilises it well. The phenoxide ion delocalises the charge onto carbon atoms of the ring, which is less effective, so carboxylic acids ionise more.
keyPoints: Carboxylate charge shared between two electronegative oxygens
Phenoxide charge sits partly on carbon
More stable anion gives stronger acid
questions.explanation: Typical pKa values are about 4.8 for ethanoic acid and 10 for phenol.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because
options: spermatogenesis needs a temperature slightly lower than body temperature
they cannot fit inside the body
questions.explanation: The scrotum keeps the testes about 2 to 3 degrees C below body temperature, which is required for sperm production.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The cell formed by the fusion of a sperm and an ovum is the
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg is the zygote, which divides repeatedly to form the embryo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the human female, FSH from the pituitary mainly
options: stimulates the growth of ovarian follicles
questions.explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone promotes the development of follicles and the secretion of oestrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a barrier method of contraception?
questions.explanation: Condoms physically block sperm from reaching the ovum and also reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The acrosome at the head of a sperm contains enzymes that
options: help the sperm penetrate the layers surrounding the ovum
determine the sex of the child
carry the nutrients to the zygote
questions.explanation: Acrosomal enzymes such as hyaluronidase digest the corona radiata and zona pellucida so that the sperm can reach the ovum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A woman who breastfeeds her baby intensively often does not ovulate for some months. This is because
options: milk contains hormones that block ovulation directly
high prolactin and the suckling reflex suppress the hormones that trigger ovulation
the ovaries are removed during lactation
questions.explanation: The suckling reflex raises prolactin and suppresses the release of gonadotropins, so ovulation and menstruation are delayed, though this is not a reliable contraceptive.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Trace the path of sperm from the testis to the outside of the body.
questions.answer: Sperms pass from the seminiferous tubules to the rete testis, then through the vasa efferentia to the epididymis, then the vas deferens, the ejaculatory duct and finally through the urethra to the outside.
keyPoints: Seminiferous tubules, rete testis, vasa efferentia
questions.explanation: Secretions of the seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands add to form semen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the role of hormones in childbirth (parturition).
questions.answer: Signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta cause mild uterine contractions, called the foetal ejection reflex. This stimulates release of oxytocin from the mother's pituitary, which causes stronger contractions, and the cycle repeats until the baby is delivered.
keyPoints: Oxytocin released from the mother's pituitary
questions.explanation: The placenta also releases relaxin, which helps soften the pelvic ligaments.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The process of copying DNA before cell division is called
questions.explanation: DNA replication produces two identical DNA molecules from one.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: An individual with the genotype Tt for a trait is called
questions.explanation: Heterozygous individuals carry two different alleles of the gene.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: A woman with blood group O marries a man with blood group AB. Which blood group can their child have?
questions.explanation: The mother can give only i; the father gives IA or IB, so the child is IAi (group A) or IBi (group B); AB and O are not possible.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The Meselson-Stahl experiment showed that DNA replication is
questions.explanation: Each new DNA molecule has one old parental strand and one newly made strand.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: In the lac operon of E. coli, when lactose is absent the repressor protein
options: binds to the operator and blocks transcription of the structural genes
binds to lactose and activates the genes
binds to the promoter and starts transcription
questions.explanation: Without an inducer the repressor sits on the operator and RNA polymerase cannot transcribe the lac genes.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Miller's experiment on the origin of life used an electric spark in a flask containing
options: methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour
questions.explanation: With these gases at about 800 degrees C, amino acids were formed, supporting the idea of chemical evolution.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Explain what is meant by the semi-conservative nature of DNA replication.
questions.answer: During replication the two strands of the parent DNA separate and each acts as a template for a new complementary strand. Every daughter DNA molecule therefore consists of one original strand and one newly synthesised strand.
keyPoints: Daughter DNA has one old and one new strand
questions.explanation: Meselson and Stahl showed this using heavy nitrogen (15N) labelling.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Why are X-linked recessive disorders such as haemophilia more common in males than in females?
questions.answer: A male has only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele on it is expressed. A female has two X chromosomes and shows the disease only if both carry the recessive allele; a carrier female with one normal allele is usually unaffected.
keyPoints: One recessive allele is enough in males
questions.explanation: Affected males inherit the allele from carrier mothers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following organisms is a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Fungi break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plasmid is
options: a circular extra-chromosomal DNA molecule in bacteria
a protein in the cell wall
questions.explanation: Plasmids replicate independently of the chromosome and are used as vectors in gene cloning.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Net primary productivity is equal to
options: gross primary productivity minus respiratory losses
the energy in the sunlight falling on the area
questions.explanation: NPP = GPP - R is the organic matter available to consumers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Green plants take up CO2 and fix it into carbohydrates during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Top carnivores are far fewer in number than herbivores in an ecosystem mainly because
options: they are larger and eat plants
energy is lost at each trophic level, so less is available at the top
questions.explanation: Only about 10 per cent of the energy passes to the next level, which limits the number of top consumers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
options: cathode (negative electrode), the larger fragments faster
anode (positive electrode), the smaller fragments faster
anode (positive electrode), the larger fragments faster
cathode (negative electrode), the smaller fragments faster
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups, so it moves toward the anode, and smaller fragments move faster through the gel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a genetically modified organism (GMO)? Mention two benefits of GM crops.
questions.answer: A GMO is a plant, animal or microbe whose genes have been altered using recombinant DNA technology. Benefits of GM crops include resistance to pests (Bt cotton), tolerance to stress, longer shelf life and enhanced nutrition such as in golden rice.
keyPoints: Organism with altered genes through rDNA technology
questions.explanation: GM crops can also reduce the use of chemical pesticides.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how Bt toxin kills insect larvae without harming the Bt crop plant.
questions.answer: The plant produces the toxin as an inactive protoxin. In the alkaline gut of the insect larva the protoxin is converted into its active form, which binds to the midgut cells, creates pores and causes them to swell and burst, killing the larva.
keyPoints: Protoxin is inactive in the plant
Pores in midgut cells cause lysis
questions.explanation: The plant cells and human gut lack the conditions or receptors that activate the toxin.

questions.subject: science

questions.q: A 5 microfarad capacitor is connected to a 12 V battery. The charge stored is
questions.explanation: Q = C V = 5 × 12 = 60 microcoulomb.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A potential difference of 200 V is applied across two parallel plates 1 cm apart. The electric field between the plates is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Two identical metal spheres carry charges +6 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb. They are touched together and then separated. The charge on each is
questions.explanation: Total charge is conserved: +4 microcoulomb shared equally by identical spheres gives +2 microcoulomb each.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A 1 microcoulomb charge moves 2 m along the direction of a uniform electric field of 500 N/C. The work done by the field is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: What is polarisation of a dielectric in an electric field?
questions.answer: When a dielectric is placed in an electric field, its molecules get a dipole moment (induced in non-polar molecules, aligned in polar ones). This gives a net surface charge that sets up a field opposing the applied field, which reduces the net field inside the dielectric.
keyPoints: Internal field opposes and reduces the applied field
questions.explanation: This is why inserting a dielectric increases capacitance.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A charged comb attracts small uncharged pieces of paper. Explain why.
questions.answer: The field of the comb polarises the paper: the nearer side acquires the opposite charge and the farther side the same charge. The field is stronger at the nearer side, so the attraction on the near charge exceeds the repulsion on the far charge and there is a net force towards the comb.
keyPoints: Paper is polarised by the comb
Opposite charge induced on near side
Non-uniform field gives a net attraction
questions.explanation: A neutral object can be attracted to a charged one because of induced charges.

questions.q: Resistors of 4 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A wire of resistance 10 ohm is cut into two equal halves, which are then joined in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: Each half has 5 ohm and two 5 ohm resistors in parallel give 2.5 ohm.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A cell of emf 6 V has an internal resistance of 0.5 ohm. The current when its terminals are short-circuited is

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with the same speed. The ratio of the radius of the alpha particle's path to that of the proton is
questions.explanation: r = m v/(q B); the alpha particle has four times the mass and twice the charge, so its radius is 4/2 = 2 times larger.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Distinguish between the emf and the terminal potential difference of a cell.
questions.answer: The emf is the potential difference between the terminals of a cell when no current is drawn (open circuit). The terminal potential difference V is measured when current I flows, and is less than the emf by the drop across the internal resistance, V = E - Ir.
keyPoints: emf is the open-circuit potential difference
Terminal pd is measured with current flowing
questions.explanation: During charging the terminal voltage is greater than the emf.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Why does placing a soft iron core inside a solenoid make its magnetic field much stronger?
questions.answer: Soft iron has a high relative permeability. The core becomes magnetised by the field of the solenoid and its magnetisation adds to the applied field, increasing the total field many times.
keyPoints: Core gets magnetised in the field
Its field adds to that of the current
questions.explanation: B = mu_0 mu_r n I with mu_r large for soft iron.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A DC motor draws a very large current at the instant it is switched on mainly because
options: the supply voltage is highest at that moment
the back emf is zero when the armature is at rest
the coil resistance is lowest then
the magnetic field is strongest then
questions.explanation: Back emf is proportional to speed; at rest it is zero, so the current is limited only by the small coil resistance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are eddy currents? State one useful application.
questions.answer: Eddy currents are circulating currents induced in a bulk piece of conductor when the magnetic flux through it changes. They are used in induction furnaces to melt metals and in electromagnetic braking of trains.
keyPoints: Induced circulating currents in solid conductors
Applications such as induction furnace or magnetic braking
questions.explanation: They also cause unwanted heating in transformer cores.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is electric power transmitted over long distances at very high voltage?
questions.answer: For a given power P = V I, a higher voltage means a smaller current. The power wasted as heat in the lines is I^2 R, so a smaller current reduces the loss greatly. Transformers step the voltage up for transmission and down for use.
keyPoints: P = VI, high V means low I
questions.explanation: Doubling the voltage cuts the line loss to one quarter for the same power.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a thin lens
options: is deviated away from the axis
questions.explanation: Near the optical centre the two faces of a thin lens are parallel, so the ray emerges without any appreciable bending.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A concave mirror forms a real image 40 cm from the mirror of an object placed 20 cm from it. The magnification is
questions.explanation: m = -v/u = -(-40)/(-20) = -2, so the image is inverted and twice the size.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A short-sighted person has a far point at 50 cm. The power of the lens needed to see distant objects clearly is
questions.explanation: A concave lens of focal length -50 cm forms a virtual image of a distant object at the far point; P = 1/(-0.5) = -2 D.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which pattern has fringes of unequal width, the central one being twice as wide as the others?
questions.explanation: In single-slit diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima, whereas Young's fringes are of equal width.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the angle of minimum deviation of a prism?
questions.answer: It is the smallest angle by which a prism can deviate a ray of light. It occurs when the ray passes symmetrically through the prism, with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of emergence.
keyPoints: Smallest deviation produced by the prism
Angle of incidence equals angle of emergence
Ray inside the prism is parallel to the base
questions.explanation: The refractive index is n = sin((A + D)/2)/sin(A/2).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a cut diamond sparkle so much?
questions.answer: Diamond has a very high refractive index (about 2.4), so its critical angle is small, about 24 degrees. Light entering the stone undergoes total internal reflection several times at the cut faces before emerging, which makes it flash brightly.
keyPoints: Repeated total internal reflection inside the stone
questions.explanation: Sin C = 1/n, so a high n gives a small critical angle.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A 1 kg ball moves at 1 m/s. Taking h = 6.63 × 10^-34 J s, its de Broglie wavelength is about
questions.explanation: lambda = h/(m v) = 6.63 × 10^-34 m, far too small to observe, which is why everyday objects show no wave behaviour.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The number of neutrons in the nucleus of uranium-235 (atomic number 92) is
questions.explanation: Neutrons = A - Z = 235 - 92 = 143.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A graph of stopping potential against frequency of incident light for a photoelectric surface is a straight line. Its slope is
questions.explanation: From e V_0 = h f - phi, V_0 = (h/e) f - phi/e, so the slope is h/e.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: In Bohr's model the speed of an electron in the n = 2 orbit compared with that in the n = 1 orbit is
questions.explanation: The orbital speed is proportional to 1/n, so it halves when n changes from 1 to 2.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: State two observations of Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment and the conclusion drawn from them.
questions.answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil, and a very small number were deflected through large angles, a few even turning back. This showed that most of the atom is empty space and that its positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.
keyPoints: A few deflected through large angles
Atom has a small dense positive nucleus
questions.explanation: The result disproved the plum-pudding model.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Why do heavy stable nuclei contain more neutrons than protons?
questions.answer: Protons repel one another by the electrostatic force, which grows as the number of protons rises. Extra neutrons add to the attractive short-range nuclear force without adding repulsion, and so help to hold a large nucleus together.
keyPoints: Proton-proton Coulomb repulsion increases with Z
questions.explanation: That is why the stability line bends above N = Z for heavy nuclei.

questions.subject: science

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of the cell constant (l/A) of a conductivity cell is
questions.explanation: Length divided by area has the unit m/m^2 = m^-1.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: For water Kb = 0.52 K kg/mol. The elevation in boiling point of a 0.2 molal solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a lead storage battery discharges, the density of the sulphuric acid electrolyte
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid is consumed to form lead sulphate at both electrodes, so the electrolyte becomes less dense.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between a primary cell and a secondary cell with one example of each.
questions.answer: A primary cell, such as a dry cell, produces current by an irreversible chemical reaction and cannot be recharged. A secondary cell, such as the lead storage battery, undergoes a reversible reaction and can be recharged by passing current in the opposite direction.
keyPoints: Primary: not rechargeable, e.g. dry cell
Secondary: rechargeable, e.g. lead storage battery
questions.explanation: A fuel cell converts the energy of fuel directly into electricity as long as fuel is supplied.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a 0.1 molal NaCl solution show nearly twice the depression of freezing point of a 0.1 molal glucose solution?
questions.answer: Freezing-point depression depends on the number of solute particles. Glucose does not dissociate, but NaCl dissociates into Na+ and Cl-, giving about twice as many particles, so the van't Hoff factor is close to 2 and the depression is nearly doubled.
keyPoints: Colligative property depends on number of particles
questions.explanation: The observed factor is slightly below 2 because of ion pairing in real solutions.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The unit of the rate constant for a second-order reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate = k[A]^2, so k = (mol L^-1 s^-1)/(mol L^-1)^2 = L mol^-1 s^-1.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: When acidified orange potassium dichromate oxidises an alcohol, the solution turns
questions.explanation: Dichromate (Cr in +6, orange) is reduced to green Cr3+.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In a reaction the rate doubles when [A] is doubled and does not change when [B] is doubled. The rate law is
questions.explanation: The rate is proportional to [A] to the first power and independent of [B].

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: For a zero-order reaction the initial concentration of the reactant is doubled. The half-life
questions.explanation: For zero order t_half = [A]0/(2k), which is proportional to the initial concentration.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: State any three characteristic properties of transition metals.
questions.answer: Transition metals show variable oxidation states, form coloured compounds and complexes, are often paramagnetic, have high melting points and densities, and act as good catalysts.
keyPoints: Catalytic activity, paramagnetism, high melting points
questions.explanation: These properties come from partly filled d orbitals.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Scandium shows only the +3 oxidation state and zinc only +2, whereas manganese shows many. Explain.
questions.answer: Scandium loses its two 4s electrons and the one 3d electron to reach the stable noble-gas configuration of Sc3+. Zinc loses only its two 4s electrons because the 3d10 subshell is stable. Manganese has five 3d and two 4s electrons of similar energy, so many different numbers can be lost.
keyPoints: Mn has many d electrons available for bonding
questions.explanation: The maximum oxidation state rises to +7 at manganese.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bidentate ligand binds to the central metal through
questions.explanation: Denticity is the number of donor atoms by which a ligand binds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The oxidation state of nickel in K2[Ni(CN)4] is
questions.explanation: Two K+ give +2, so the complex ion is 2-; four CN- give -4, so nickel is +2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 is
questions.explanation: Six aqua ligands and chromium in the +3 state with three chloride counter ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 and [Cr(H2O)5Cl]Cl2.H2O are examples of which type of isomerism?
questions.explanation: The isomers differ in the number of water molecules inside and outside the coordination sphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of the high-spin complex [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (four unpaired electrons) is about
questions.explanation: mu = root(4 × 6) = root 24, which is about 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the IUPAC name of [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2.
questions.answer: Pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride. Five ammine ligands, one chlorido ligand, cobalt in the +3 state, and two chloride counter ions.
keyPoints: Ligands named alphabetically: ammine then chlorido
questions.explanation: The oxidation state is found from the total charge of +2 on the cation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How is EDTA used in the estimation of hardness of water?
questions.answer: EDTA forms very stable, soluble complexes with Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions. The hard water is titrated with a standard EDTA solution using an indicator, and the volume used gives the total concentration of these ions.
keyPoints: EDTA is a hexadentate chelating ligand
Forms stable complexes with Ca2+ and Mg2+
questions.explanation: The indicator changes colour when all the metal ions have been complexed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an aryl halide?
questions.explanation: In an aryl halide the halogen is bonded directly to an sp2 carbon of an aromatic ring.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which reagent oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without further oxidation to the acid?
questions.explanation: PCC is a mild oxidising agent that stops at the aldehyde stage.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid at low temperature gives
options: a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol
questions.explanation: The -OH group directs the incoming group to the ortho and para positions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which isomer of nitrophenol is steam volatile?
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so it is less associated and volatile, whereas p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Methylmagnesium bromide reacts with methanal, and the product is hydrolysed. The final product is
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents add to methanal to give primary alcohols with one more carbon, here CH3CH2OH.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reactions in terms of kinetics.
questions.answer: SN1 is a two-step reaction through a carbocation and its rate depends only on the haloalkane concentration, so it is first order. SN2 occurs in one step with the nucleophile attacking from the back, so its rate depends on both haloalkane and nucleophile and it is second order.
keyPoints: Rate of SN2 depends on nucleophile concentration
questions.explanation: Tertiary halides favour SN1 and primary halides favour SN2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does the boiling point of haloalkanes increase in the order RCl < RBr < RI for the same alkyl group?
questions.answer: The size and molar mass of the halogen increase from Cl to I, so the molecule has a larger surface area and more polarisable electrons. The van der Waals forces between molecules become stronger, and more energy is needed to separate them.
keyPoints: Larger halogen means greater molar mass and surface area
questions.explanation: For isomeric haloalkanes branching lowers the boiling point.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Methanoic acid (formic acid) is naturally present in
questions.explanation: The name comes from the Latin word for ant; it is injected in ant stings.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanal on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride gives
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are reduced to primary alcohols.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aniline treated with nitrous acid (NaNO2 and HCl) at 0 to 5 degrees C gives
questions.explanation: Primary aromatic amines form diazonium salts at low temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives an equimolar mixture of
questions.explanation: The mixture, called invert sugar, is laevorotatory because fructose is strongly laevorotatory.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The alpha and beta forms of D-glucose are called anomers because they differ in configuration at
questions.explanation: They differ only in the orientation of the -OH group at the anomeric carbon C1 formed in ring closure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between fibrous and globular proteins with an example of each.
questions.answer: Fibrous proteins have long thread-like polypeptide chains held side by side, are insoluble in water and serve structural roles, for example keratin and myosin. Globular proteins fold into a spherical shape, are soluble in water and perform functions such as catalysis, for example enzymes and insulin.
keyPoints: Globular: spherical, water soluble, e.g. insulin
questions.explanation: The shape is decided by the secondary and tertiary structure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are aliphatic amines stronger bases than ammonia in the gas phase?
questions.answer: Alkyl groups release electrons by the +I effect, which increases the electron density on nitrogen. The lone pair is then more available to accept a proton, and the ammonium ion formed is stabilised by the alkyl groups, so alkylamines are stronger bases than ammonia.
questions.explanation: In water, solvation and steric effects change the order among primary, secondary and tertiary amines.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The release of the ovum from the Graafian follicle is called
questions.explanation: Ovulation occurs around the middle of the menstrual cycle.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Yeast reproduces asexually mainly by
questions.explanation: A small bud grows out of the parent cell and separates to form a new yeast cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gametes in humans are formed by
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, producing haploid gametes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many pollen mother cells must undergo meiosis to produce 100 pollen grains?
questions.explanation: Each pollen mother cell gives four haploid pollen grains, so 100/4 = 25 are needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the human male, luteinising hormone acts on the
questions.explanation: LH stimulates the Leydig (interstitial) cells, whereas FSH acts on the Sertoli cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is parturition?
questions.answer: Parturition is the process of giving birth, in which the fully developed foetus is expelled from the uterus through the vagina at the end of pregnancy, brought about by powerful uterine contractions.
keyPoints: Controlled by hormones such as oxytocin
questions.explanation: In humans pregnancy lasts about nine months.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the role of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?
questions.answer: hCG is secreted by the developing placental tissue. It maintains the corpus luteum so that it keeps secreting progesterone, which preserves the endometrium and prevents menstruation. It is also the basis of pregnancy tests.
questions.explanation: Later the placenta itself secretes enough progesterone.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Which type of RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA brings specific amino acids and reads the codon through its anticodon.
