questions.q: How many different types of gametes can an individual of genotype AaBb produce, assuming independent assortment?
questions.explanation: AB, Ab, aB and ab are formed in equal numbers.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Mendel's law of independent assortment holds good for genes that are
options: very close on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: Genes on different chromosomes assort independently during meiosis; closely linked genes tend to be inherited together.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Morgan's work on Drosophila showed that genes located close together on the same chromosome
options: show linkage and a low frequency of recombination
are always on the X chromosome
questions.explanation: Linked genes are inherited together more often than expected, and the closer they are the lower the recombination frequency.

questions.explanation: Aa × Aa gives 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, so one in four is affected.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: What are mutations? Name two types.
questions.answer: Mutations are sudden heritable changes in the DNA of an organism. They include point mutations, which change a single base pair (such as in sickle-cell anaemia), and chromosomal mutations such as deletion, duplication or changes in chromosome number.
questions.explanation: Mutations are a source of variation for evolution.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: What is adaptive radiation? Give one example.
questions.answer: Adaptive radiation is the evolution of many different forms from a common ancestor in one geographical area, each adapted to a different habitat or way of life. Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Islands, with differently shaped beaks, are an example.
keyPoints: Example Darwin's finches or Australian marsupials
questions.explanation: It is a process of divergent evolution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plasmid vector such as pBR322 contains genes for
options: antibiotic resistance, which act as selectable markers
questions.explanation: Antibiotic-resistance genes allow selection of the bacteria that have taken up the plasmid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of a water sample indicates
options: water rich in dissolved oxygen only
questions.explanation: BOD is the oxygen used by microbes to break down organic matter, so a high value means heavy organic pollution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Water hyacinth is a serious problem in Indian water bodies because it
options: grows very rapidly and depletes oxygen, harming aquatic life
adds extra oxygen to the water
questions.explanation: It is an invasive alien species that forms dense mats, blocking light and lowering dissolved oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the gene gun (biolistics) method of gene transfer into plant cells, the DNA is
options: coated on microscopic gold or tungsten particles fired into the cells
injected into the nucleus with a fine needle
added with calcium ions to bacteria
questions.explanation: High-velocity microparticles coated with DNA are shot through the cell wall into plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two methods of ex situ conservation.
questions.answer: Examples are zoos and botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks and cryopreservation of gametes at very low temperature in liquid nitrogen.
questions.explanation: These methods safeguard endangered species outside their natural habitats.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain the greenhouse effect and name one consequence of its enhancement.
questions.answer: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorb the infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-radiate part of it back, keeping the planet warm. Increased emissions from human activity strengthen this effect and cause global warming, leading to melting of ice and rising sea level.
keyPoints: Enhancement causes global warming and sea-level rise
questions.explanation: Without the natural greenhouse effect the Earth would be much colder.
